description: One of the largest bony fish in the world, the Atlantic Bluefin Tuna is a highly migratory apex predator. It undertakes seasonal migrations between feeding grounds in the North Atlantic and spawning areas in the Mediterranean Sea and Gulf of Mexico.
notes: T_mid raised to 22.0°C (peak spawning range 22–24°C, maximum larval survival rate). Range 15–25°C covers combined feeding and spawning phase in the Mediterranean. Radius 200km = conservative safety margin for 48h window (50km/day migration).

description: A commercially vital groundfish of the North Atlantic, Atlantic Cod prefers cold, deep waters and is highly sensitive to temperature changes. Populations have declined sharply due to overfishing, making real-time vessel overlap monitoring especially critical for this species.
notes: temp_max set to 12.0°C — critical metabolic tipping point (aerobic scope collapses above 12°C). temp_range adjusted to 6.0°C (0–12°C habitat, optimum 0–6°C during spawning). T_mid=6.0°C correlates with optimal embryonic development (~14 days at 6°C). Radius 100km appropriate for site-faithful species.

description: A small, fast-reproducing pelagic fish found along European Atlantic coasts and throughout the Mediterranean. European Sardines form extremely dense schools and are a keystone forage species in the marine food web, making their spawning grounds particularly vulnerable to fishing pressure.
notes: Range 10–20°C scientifically precise (10°C isotherm north, 20°C isotherm south). Spawning at 13–18°C, larval habitat 16–18°C SST. temp_range adjusted to 5.0°C (narrower thermal optimum). Radius 50km strategic for false-alarm minimisation given locally dense schools. Schools at 25–55m depth during day, 10–35m at night.

description: A large, highly migratory predatory fish recognisable by its long, flat bill. Swordfish undergo diel vertical migration — staying at depths of 400–600m during the day and surfacing at night — meaning interactions with fishing fleets occur predominantly during nighttime hours.
notes: Range 18–28°C correct: adults prefer 18–22°C SST (epipelagic phase), larvae/juveniles >24°C. T_mid=23.0°C (lingering behaviour at 23–27°C = potential spawning grounds). Radius 150km covers 48h window (30–55km/day normal transit, max. 107km/day). Diel vertical migration: 400–600m daytime, surface at night — fleet interaction primarily nocturnal.
